policy.reuse_rule: Borrow behavior from several sources, but keep one product visual language.
policy.license_rule: A reference link is not permission to copy source code; verify the pinned package license before code reuse.

patterns.title: Project graph as home
apply: Keep the active path visible
Use status labels as well as color
Open detail without replacing the graph
Collapse completed or secondary groups
avoid: Treating every datum as a node
Using animation without an execution meaning
Hiding blocked work with filters

patterns.title: Stable overview with detail inspector
jobs: inspect one item without losing context
apply: Persist selection
Lead with the decision-relevant summary
Step down to evidence and source
Keep close and keyboard navigation explicit
avoid: Opening a new page for every detail
Showing internal IDs before human-readable meaning
Relying on hover

patterns.title: Human attention queue
jobs: see only decisions requiring human attention
apply: Name the requested decision
Show urgency and consequence
Group duplicate notifications
Remove the item when its underlying state resolves
avoid: Asking whether generic output was useful
Using notification count as importance
Interrupting for agent-resolvable work

patterns.title: Review before completion
jobs: approve or request a concrete change
apply: Show what changed
Bind evidence to the exact revision
Separate pass evidence from limitations
Offer approve and request-changes dispositions
avoid: Equating green tests with human acceptance
Making the reviewer reconstruct the change from raw files
Hiding non-claims

patterns.title: Completion receipt and next step
apply: State the completed outcome
Give the exact evidence identity
Explain what happens next
Keep limitations adjacent
avoid: Celebratory status without evidence
Calling a supporting artifact the user outcome
Adding a feedback survey as the default next step

patterns.title: Task list with meaningful progress
apply: Group tasks by outcome
Show prerequisite state
Use action labels rather than generic status
Keep completed tasks available but quiet
avoid: Treating activity count as progress
Presenting blocked tasks as actionable
Duplicating one task across views

patterns.title: Overview first, evidence on demand
jobs: scan a large body of work
apply: Reserve the first screen for status and decisions
Use parameters to reduce density
Make update time visible
Coordinate overview and detail selection
avoid: A wall of equally weighted cards
Decorative metrics
Requiring scrolling before the active decision is visible

patterns.title: Honest unavailable state
jobs: know what would make the view available
apply: Name the missing source or contract
Preserve the unavailable control
Give the resume event
Do not substitute stale data silently
avoid: Blank panels
Fabricated placeholders that look live
Removing unavailable views from navigation

patterns.title: Linked work and system lenses
jobs: compare the plan with the system being changed
navigate between work and architecture without conflating them
apply: Name the question answered by each lens
Keep edge semantics distinct per lens
Carry stable semantic selection across views
Keep one inspector and provenance grammar
avoid: Combining work dependencies and system interfaces in one graph
Calling a work graph an architecture diagram
Changing the selected subject silently when switching lenses

patterns.title: Architecture from context to components
jobs: inspect components and contracts at the useful level
apply: Show current and proposed elements distinctly
Name boundary ownership
Label arrows by their exact relationship
Expose contracts and material omissions in the inspector
avoid: One diagram containing every abstraction level
Unlabeled arrows
Boxes with no owner or contract meaning

patterns.title: Requirement-to-evidence assurance map
jobs: judge whether a plan is complete
find requirements without architecture, work, risks, or credible evidence
apply: Trace each criterion to architecture, work, and evidence
Distinguish covered, partial, and missing
Keep assessor questions next to the criterion
Separate machine checks from human acceptance
avoid: Using a single completion percentage
Treating test presence as proof of the requirement
Hiding unknowns in footnotes

patterns.title: Plan-to-code conformance review
jobs: compare implemented code with the planned architecture
identify drift and unsupported completion claims
apply: Name the planned obligation that changed
Link changed artifacts and exact revision
Show checks and observed behavior separately
Surface drift and non-claims before approval
avoid: Reviewing code without the intended architecture
Equating passing tests with conformance
Showing a diff without the requirement it is meant to satisfy
